title: The Unequal Opportunities of Large Language Models: Revealing Demographic Bias through Job Recommendations

bias_targets.methodology: Using counterfactual pronoun substitution (he/him/his vs. she/her/hers) in prompt templates requesting job recommendations and salaries, then applying text clustering and analyzing the probability distributions and median wages of jobs recommended to men versus women.

Substituting 20 different country names in job recommendation prompts to indicate a candidate's nationality, then analyzing the differences in suggested job clusters and median salary distributions across the different nationalities.

Combining specific gender pronouns and nationalities in job recommendation prompts to measure compounded biases by analyzing the ratio of job recommendations and median salaries across the intersections of gender identity and nationality.
